paper_title: SOS Lower Bounds with Hard Constraints: Think Global, Act Local
classifications: Theory of computation → Randomness, geometry and discrete structures
statement: Finally, we leave as open one more “hard constraint” challenge that arises even in the simple context of random 3XOR or 3SAT. Suppose one tried to refute random mconstraint 3XOR instances by trying to refute the following statement for all quadruples (k001 , k010 , k100 , k111 ) that sum to m: “exactly ka constraints are satisfied with assignment a”, for each a ∈ {001, 010, 100, 111}.
context: ITCS 2019 Finally, we leave as open one more “hard constraint” challenge that arises even in the simple context of random 3XOR or 3SAT. Suppose one tried to refute random mconstraint 3XOR instances by trying to refute the following statement for all quadruples (k001 , k010 , k100 , k111 ) that sum to m: “exactly ka constraints are satisfied with assignment a”, for each a ∈ {001, 010, 100, 111}. As far as we know, constant-degree SOS may succeed with this strategy when m = O(n). It is natural to believe that there is (whp) an Ω(n)-degree SOS pseudodistribution that satisfies all of the above constraints with pseudovariance zero when k001 = k010 = k100 = k111 = m/4, but we do not know how to construct one.
